The '''Belcanto Campaign''' was the Vesperan conquest of the Belcantese states from 1892 to 1895. It ended Belcantese independence and began more than fifty years of Vesperan occupation.

== Background ==

The Belcantese states controlled important ports, mineral areas, forest regions, and trade routes. Their federal system and difficult terrain had allowed them to resist earlier conquest attempts. By the 1890s, the expanding [[Vesperan Empire]] viewed Belcanto as both a strategic prize and a potential base for anti-Vesperan alignment.

The old source identifies the [[Belcantese-Northern Alliance Treaty of 1891]] as the immediate trigger for Vesperan action. Vesperan intelligence treated closer Belcantese ties with anti-imperial powers as a threat.

== Campaign ==

The invasion combined naval assault, coastal consolidation, forest warfare, siege operations, and mountain campaigning. Vesperan forces used superior naval power and specialized siege artillery, while Belcantese forces relied on fortifications, local terrain, militia networks, and delaying actions.

The [[Siege of Belgrad]] became the central operation of the forest campaign. The campaign ended in Vesperan victory and the annexation of Belcantese territory. [[Belgrad]] was occupied, and Vesperan authorities began replacing local federal institutions with imperial administration.

== Aftermath ==

The occupation redirected Belcanto's economy into the Vesperan imperial system. Cultural policy, including the [[Imperial Cultural Integration Decree of 1897]], attempted to suppress Belcantese traditions, especially public performances and local-language institutions.

These policies failed to erase Belcantese identity. Instead, they helped create the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]], which later became a model for underground organization in occupied territories.

== Legacy ==

The campaign became one of the clearest examples of Vesperan occupation before the [[Avant Great War]]. Its long-term effect was not only conquest but the creation of a resistance culture that reemerged during the empire's collapse in 1949.
